lens: Pipeline-native: practice tied to real deal stages in a kanban, rehearse tomorrow's real call
name: Pipeline Rehearsal Console
one_liner: A pipeline-first, dark-by-default cockpit: practice is organized around the deals a rep actually works, a provisional rubric and whisper coach run during the call, and a faceted library of about 180 personas is extended by contributors through a guided wizard.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the pipeline-native lens: the home is a kanban of deal stages where each card has a Rehearse button, and any practice call (pre-built or wizard-made) can attach to a deal. Changed two things. A sales kanban does not fit collections, recruiting or customer success, so the board generalizes into job-specific lanes (aging buckets, screen-to-offer, renewal windows) and the library covers every job. The lens also had no live coaching, so I added a coach lane and a provisional rubric rail. Research: a MindTickle comparison says Second Nature does not turn live calls into new practice, which supports the calls-to-practice loop. Hyperbound lists Live Call Coaching as a private preview, so the window is open but closing.

design_language.typography: Sora 600 and 700 for headlines, Inter 400, 500 and 600 for UI and transcripts, JetBrains Mono 500 with tabular numerals for timers, scores and cue timestamps. Scale 12, 14, 16, 20, 28, 40. Body is 16px minimum on mobile; all text meets WCAG AA 4.5:1.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Radius 14px for cards, 10px for controls, pill shapes for chips and facet tags. Hairline 1px borders instead of heavy shadows; elevation only for floating cues and sheets. In dark mode, surfaces step up in lightness rather than casting shadows. 12-column grid on desktop, 4-column on mobile, 16px gutters.
design_language.motion: State changes at 180 to 220ms ease-out. Coach cues slide up and fade in over 240ms and are capped at one per 20 seconds. The score ring tweens over 600ms. Kanban drags use layout animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion, everything falls back to opacity changes.
design_language.iconography: Lucide at 1.75px stroke. Status always pairs icon and text, never color alone. Coach cues use a spark glyph; personas use generated monogram avatars with a hue derived from the persona id, not stock photos.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark is the default for Live Call and Debrief; light is the default for Pipeline, Library, Progress and Team. Both respect prefers-color-scheme and offer a toggle. Tokens are defined on :root with overrides under [data-theme=dark] and the media query guarded by :root:not([data-theme=light]).

navigation_and_ia: Top bar: Pipeline (home when signed in), Library, Progress, Team (manager role only), a Cmd-K button and a Demo chip. The public landing page is a README-style hero. Routes: / (landing), /pipeline, /library, /library/new (wizard), /practice/[persona] (pre-call briefing), /call/[id] (live call), /debrief/[id], /progress, /team. Live call and pre-call hide the global nav and show a breadcrumb back to the deal. A Demo mode runs without login, starting on the Dana Whitfield persona. Existing routes stay, so existing links keep working.

screens.layout: Full-bleed hero: headline and CTAs on the left, a real product frame on the right showing the live call with the rubric rail and one coach cue. Below it: a three-step strip (Pipeline, Call, Debrief), a row of 12 persona tiles with facet pills, a model stack line, and a contributor band with a Codex CLI prompt to copy and a good-first-issue count. The README mirrors this hero.
screens.key_components: Headline 'Rehearse the call you have tomorrow.' Primary button Try the demo, secondary Run locally. MIT badge, GitHub stars, live demo link. Model stack chips are plain text (Realtime voice, gpt-realtime, grading gpt-4.1-mini, wizard structured outputs), not OpenAI logos.

screens.layout: Four-step stepper across the top: Source, Persona, Scenario and rubric, Test call. One focused panel per step with a live preview card on the right. Source accepts a pasted or dropped job description, product URL, CRM note, ICP text or a real call transcript, redacted before sending.

screens.change_vs_today: Replaces the manual scenario form with a guided, reviewable generation flow that still lets the user edit every field.

screens.layout: Two columns. Left: a deal card (company, stage, last call summary, 'fix next time' items pulled from the last debrief) and a persona brief (who they are, what they want, three likely objections, three must-hit points). Right: a briefing card with a stacked rubric-weight bar, talk-track checklist, mic check meter, Voice/Text toggle and Start call.

screens.layout: Three columns on 1440px. Left 280px: talk-track stepper (done, now, next), goal, persona presence card with emotion meter and audio-reactive ring. Center: transcript in three lanes (persona in teal, rep in neutral, coach cues in violet between turns). Right 340px: provisional rubric rail (score ring tagged provisional, five criterion rows with 1-to-5 chips and status) and a Next best question card. Bottom bar: waveform, timer, cue budget, mute, End and grade.
screens.key_components: Cue types: next question, objection alert with a hint such as acknowledge then value, talk-track step complete, pace or filler warning. Each cue is one line with a Why expander. Whisper audio is optional and off by default. The persona never sees coach text.
screens.change_vs_today: Replaces the chat app with a coached cockpit. The persona's behavior does not change; the rep gains real-time feedback.

screens.layout: Top: grade ring with the numeric score first, a band label, and a goal-result chip. A status pill reads Heuristic estimate when the LLM grader fails, with an explanation tooltip. screens.change_vs_today: Replaces one long vertical scroll with a scannable top, a timeline and drill-down evidence.

screens.layout: Single column. Top: persona name, timer, End call with a confirm step. The transcript fills the screen with the last two turns visible. The latest coach cue sits as a one-line card above the composer. A bottom sheet, dragged up, holds the rubric rail and talk-track stepper. The composer has 16px text, a large mic button and send.
screens.key_components: Sheet snap points at 64px, 50% and 90%. Cue arrival gets a haptic tap where supported. Controls sit in the thumb zone. Sticky composer. No horizontal scroll at any width.
screens.change_vs_today: Replaces the chat-only mobile screen, which has no rubric or talk track, with a coached layout that still fits one hand.

live_coaching_and_scoring: The coach runs in a separate channel from the persona, so the persona stays in character. After each rep turn, a gpt-4.1-mini call receives the rubric, talk track and recent transcript, and returns structured JSON: criterion deltas, provisional scores and at most one cue. Cue budget is one per 20 seconds, with no more than three high-priority cues per call. Scores are labelled provisional until the final grade, and the debrief shows the quote that moved each score. Latency target is under 1.5 seconds from turn end to cue. In voice mode the persona runs on the Realtime API while the coach reads the text transcript in parallel.
persona_library_and_wizard: The library ships about 180 personas as one JSON file each under /personas, validated by zod in CI. They span 14 job families (SDR cold call, AE discovery, renewal CS, collections, recruiting, procurement, service desk and more) and 16 industries (SaaS, insurance, mortgage, real estate, solar, home services, auto, medical devices and more). Facets are job, industry, difficulty, objection type, channel and length. The wizard runs Source, Persona, Scenario and rubric, Test call, using structured outputs against the same zod schema. The output is previewed and editable before it is saved locally or proposed as a PR. URL fetching in the Source step uses a server-side allowlist and a size cap.
signature_moments: A Next best question card that appears while the rep is missing a discovery point, with the talk-track step ticking over.
Rubric chips filling in during the call, each marked provisional until the debrief confirms it with a quote.
A pipeline card that shows its last rehearsal score and a Rehearse tomorrow's call button.
A Moments timeline in the debrief that scrubs the call and shows what the coach said at each point.
The wizard's What we read chips, which prove the AI actually extracted facts from the job posting or URL.
openai_fund_angle: The UI shows OpenAI models where they do work. A model stack line sits on the landing page and in every debrief footer: Voice gpt-realtime, Coach gpt-4.1-mini, Grader gpt-4.1-mini, Wizard structured outputs, each with per-call estimated cost, so reviewers see real usage. The wizard's Show schema toggle makes structured outputs visible. For contributors, every persona card has Improve this persona, which opens a PR template, and an Add persona with Codex button that copies a prompt for the Codex CLI. A Reviewed with Codex badge appears only if the repo really uses Codex for PR review, which matches the Codex for Open Source criteria (PR review, maintainer automation, release workflows). A /contribute page shows maintainer activity and commit cadence, since the program is for active maintainers. Use model names as plain text and no OpenAI logo, to respect brand rules.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0 (about 3 days): add tokens on :root with dark overrides, initialize shadcn/ui, swap in Sora, Inter and JetBrains Mono, stay on Tailwind v3. Phase 1 (2 to 3 weeks): rebuild pre-call, live call and debrief on the new components and remove three.js from the call route. Phase 2 (about 2 weeks): library with about 180 seeded personas, facets and the wizard. Phase 3 (about 2 weeks): pipeline board, dashboard, manager view, mobile sheet, then Tailwind v4. Keep existing routes and data shapes; add pipeline and persona tables additively in Prisma.

risks: Coach latency and cost: a second model call per turn can add delay and spend. Mitigate with the cue budget, a text-only coach and a visible cost line.
Provisional live scores can mislead a rep. Label them clearly and make the debrief the only final grade.
AI-generated personas can encode stereotypes about accent, gender, ethnicity or income. Add a review checklist and bias checks in CI before any seeded persona ships.
Recording consent: pasted or imported real calls need a consent step, and two-party-consent states apply.
The pipeline lens needs deal data. Ship CSV and ICS import in the OSS core; keep HubSpot and Salesforce connectors as paid or contributor-built.
Scope: nine screens plus a kanban is a lot. Phase 1 must prove the live call end to end before the library and team surfaces are built.
OpenAI brand use: plain-text model names only, no logos without approval.
self_scores: A Look 8.0; B UX 7.5; C Unique 7.0; D Live coaching and scoring 6.0 (exceeds the 5.0 baseline only if the 1.5 second latency and cue budget hold); E Persona library and wizard 6.0 (depends on shipping and reviewing about 180 personas); F1 SaaS viability 4 (crowded market, free OSS core undercuts paid tiers); F2 selling to entities 6 (training firms and call centers buy persona packs, white-label and SSO); F3 not worth it 3 (clearly worth building).
